subject: Evaluation milestones, MAP and private-offer conversion plan for BrightCart
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Singh <alice.singh@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed evaluation milestones & private-offer conversion plan

Hi Alice / BrightCart procurement team,

Great speaking on Friday — thanks for the time. Per our conversation, I put together a concise evaluation milestone plan that ties to a staged private-offer pricing cadence so you can pilot Redwood Inference in production-like scenarios and convert to a committed private offer if the metrics look good.

High level (attached):
- 2-week technical spike (POC): baseline perf & integration checklist; target 100k inference requests/day equivalent
- 4-week pilot: workload parity tests, KV cache warmup, latency SLO verification
- 8-week ramp to production: throughput scaling, autoscaling policy validation

Suggested MAP-linked economics:
- Pilot credits: $50k in marketplace credit on sign-up to cover pilot usage
- Commit tranche 1 (first 6 months): 10% off list with a 6-month $X commit after pilot success
- Commit tranche 2 (annual): step-down pricing to 15% off at $Y annual commit / regional SLA add-on

I attached a short MAP doc with milestones + acceptance criteria and a starter pricing ladder. If that looks reasonable I can route a private-offer draft through AWS Marketplace (or Azure/GCP if you prefer) and include DocuSign for signatures.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm acceptance criteria for pilot by Wed, Jul 21
2) Redwood provides an updated pricing ladder and marketplace private-offer draft by Thu, Jul 22
3) Pilot kickoff the week of Jul 26

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_MAP_BrightCart_v1.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)] [Attachment: pricing-ladder-brightcart.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)]

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Singh <alice.singh@brightcart.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed evaluation milestones & private-offer conversion plan

Sofia,

Thanks — this is exactly what we need to accelerate the evaluation. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Acceptance criteria: for us the core gating items are (1) 99th pctl latency not degrading by more than 20% vs current baseline, and (2) inference cost per 1k tokens no more than 0.85x of our current provider after caching.
- Timeline: we can start the POC on Jul 27 but procurement will need the private-offer draft to include the pilot credits and a 30-day cancellation clause; legal will want a short term-of-service clause for the pilot window.
- Discount triggers: Procurement prefers a staggered rebate (credit on invoice) tied to hitting throughput milestones rather than upfront discounts. Can you model rebate mechanics against the tranches?

One other ask: can you include both an AWS Marketplace private-offer path and a backup Azure Offer path (we may run the pilot on both clouds in parallel).

If you send an updated MAP and the rebate model by Thu we can loop in legal and get an internal OK to proceed with the POC.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Singh
Head of Cloud, BrightCart
alice.singh@brightcart.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BrightCart — rebate model + pilot ask (need pricing ladder + marketplace path)

Team — forwarding BrightCart asks below. Key asks: model a rebate (credit on invoice) tied to throughput milestones instead of straight upfront discount; include AWS private-offer and Azure fallback; include a 30-day pilot cancellation clause and short pilot term.

Questions for pricing:
- Can we map a three-tranche rebate ladder (pilot -> 6m commit -> annual) where rebate is applied retroactively each month once a tranche threshold is achieved?
- What are the minimum commit levels that make sense for us to provide the 10% and 15% economics?
- Any concerns about offering a marketplace private offer that can be converted to a regional Dedicated reservation later?

I attached the MAP + starter ladder. Need a quick spreadsheet update and a one-pager we can send to procurement by Thu, Jul 22.

Thanks — Sofia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightCart — rebate model + pilot ask (need pricing ladder + marketplace path)

Sofia / team,

Attached is a proposed pricing ladder and a simple rebate mechanism that implements retroactive credits once milestone thresholds are met. Highlights:

- Pilot: $50k marketplace credit as Sofia proposed; no commitment.
- Tranche A (6-month commit): $250k committed spend -> 8% rebate applied monthly once threshold met; rebate appears on the following invoice as a credit.
- Tranche B (12-month commit): $750k annual commit -> cumulative 15% rebate; step-down per unit pricing to reflect scale; regional SLA add-on available at +$X/month.
- Rebate mechanics: Monthly measurement window; once consumed tokens pass tranche threshold for the month, rebate is computed retroactively and credited on next invoice. If they fall below the tranche in any subsequent month, prior credits remain (no clawback).

Marketplace mechanics: we can publish a private offer on AWS with those credits and commitments; Azure requires an MS commercial terms review but we can publish a similar offer there as a single-tenant plan.

Two operational notes:
1) For the rebate to be simple we recommend measuring against billable inference units (post-cache) rather than raw tokens.
2) Legal will want language around audit rights and measurement methodology in the private-offer terms.

Attachment: [Attachment: pricing-ladder-brightcart.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)]

Marcus Lin
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Singh <alice.singh@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed evaluation milestones & private-offer conversion plan

Alice / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for confirming the pilot start cadence. Per Marcus' pricing ladder (attached), we updated the MAP to reflect the rebate-on-invoice approach and included both an AWS Marketplace private-offer path and an Azure fallback. Key points in the updated MAP:

- Pilot (week 0–2): $50k marketplace credit; acceptance criteria as you specified (99th pctl latency & cost target)
- If acceptance criteria met, BrightCart signs the 6-month tranche A commit (recommended $250k) and rebates apply retroactively monthly once thresholds are met
- If the 12-month commitment is executed within the first 90 days of production we provide the larger 15% effective rebate and region-specific SLA add-on option

Attached: Redwood_MAP_BrightCart_v1.pdf (MAP + acceptance criteria) and pricing-ladder-brightcart.xlsx. I also created a DocuSign envelope for the private-offer draft so procurement/legal can review and sign. Link: https://www.docusign.net/transactions/details/0A3B4C5D6E7F

Let me know if you want a short call Thurs afternoon to run the MAP line-by-line; otherwise if procurement/legal approve the language we can publish the AWS private offer and get the pilot credits applied before Jul 27.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
